---
title: "Sources, credit, and student contributions"
---

## Previous placement work

The [Neuroimaging Guide](https://neuroimaging-guide.netlify.app/) was created by a previous placement student and helped identify topics for this programme. Donggyurim’s training pathway has new explanations, a different learning structure, and supervisor checkpoints. We recognise the earlier student’s contribution without claiming authorship of their guide.

No text, code implementation, screenshots, research figures, interactive viewer, or numerical findings from that guide have been imported. No explicit reuse licence was found on the inspected public pages on 5 October 2026; that does not establish who owns the rights or whether permission exists elsewhere.

The new lessons cite official tool documentation. Source verification and successful website rendering do not amount to end-to-end practical validation.

## Adding earlier work later

Confirm the rights holder and the relevant placement/institutional agreement. Obtain written permission or an applicable licence before importing protected material. Agree the scope of reuse, edits, public hosting, onward contributions, and credit. Check separately for third-party content and dataset restrictions.

Attribution does not replace permission. Do not describe paraphrasing as a guarantee against copyright claims. General ideas and methods can inform independently written teaching, but copying substantial protected expression may still raise issues even without identical wording. See [IP Australia’s copyright guidance](https://ipfirstresponse.ipaustralia.gov.au/options/infringement-101-copyright-infringement) and [ownership guidance](https://www.ipaustralia.gov.au/understanding-ip/who-owns-ip). Ask your institution to resolve uncertain ownership or agreement terms.

## New student contributions

Before substantial work begins, agree how contributions may be used, edited, published, and credited. Record consent through the institution’s approved process. A commit or pull request alone should not be treated as a blanket copyright transfer. This repository currently has no blanket content licence; do not apply one retrospectively to other contributors’ material without authority.

Keep signed agreements and personal correspondence out of the public repository. The supervisor may add an agreed public credit once the student has confirmed their preferred name and wording.
